content.comment_body: I need to trigger a block output for 0.1 seconds after the input signal switches to 0. I haven't found any single logic block that accomplishes this. My current workaround is to use an XOR block with an off-delay timer and my input. When the input goes to 0, the off-delay timer triggers the XOR output for 0.1 seconds. I am searching for a solution that uses just one block.
Hello, If triggering the output at first scan after start-up (and input = 0) isn't an issue, you can use a Wiping Relay. Simply invert the trigger input. You can refer to the attached image. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: The user finds it challenging to create a 0.1-second output pulse after an input signal turns off using the available logic blocks, noting the absence of a single-block solution. They currently combine XOR and off-delay timer blocks to achieve the desired output, indicating interest in a more streamlined or integrated approach within the logic programming platform.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to address the issue using a straightforward and built-in function block, eliminating the need for a workaround that requires multiple logic blocks.
